facts.text: I rewatched "La La Land" on Amazon Prime on the day of my message.
I am looking for movie recommendations.
I have seen most of the suggested movies.
I have been meaning to rewatch "Chicago" for a while.
I watched a play on Disney+, "Hamilton".
I loved the musical numbers and the story of "Hamilton" on Disney+.
I had been wanting to see "Hamilton" for years.
I watched "Hamilton" twice in one week.
I convinced my family to watch "Hamilton" with me the second time around.
The way the story was told through music and dance resonated with me and my family.
Lin-Manuel Miranda used hip-hop and R&B to tell the story of American history in "Hamilton".
The cast's energy and performances were incredible to me.
I believe "Hamilton" conveys the theme that America's story is complex and multifaceted.
I believe "Hamilton" shows that the voices and experiences of people of color are an integral part of America's story.
I believe the show humanizes the Founding Fathers and shows they were flawed individuals who made mistakes.
I believe the show also shows the Founding Fathers had hopes and dreams for the country.
I think "Hamilton" resonates with contemporary audiences because it feels more honest and authentic than the traditional, sanitized version of American history learned in school.
I think "Hamilton" is a reminder that the country's history is messy and complicated.
I think "Hamilton" emphasizes acknowledging and learning from mistakes to move forward.
I think the show's themes of ambition, love, and legacy are universally relatable.
I think the music in "Hamilton" is catchy and infectious.
